newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus border guards halt top Lukashenko opponent.
newsitem.headline: Belarus border guards halt top Lukashenko opponent.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko's most prominent opponent said on Saturday Belarus border guards had barred him from leaving for a visit to Poland and told him his documents were invalid.
Semyon Sharetsky, head of parliament until Lukashenko disbanded it under his controversial new constitution, told Reuters he was turned back at the border town of Grodno on Friday.
"I wanted to meet the speaker of the Polish parliament, Jozef Zych, as we have become good friends," Sharetsky said.

Sharetsky, elected in 1995, said he had been told he had no right to keep his diplomatic passport and that he should go back to Minsk and re-register his service passport, issued to officials in the former Soviet republic of 10 million.
"I was told the diplomatic passport could only be held by the 110 deputies of the new parliament," he said.
He said he would ask the foreign ministry for an explanation but declined to comment on whether the incident was politically motivated and stressed the trip was a private one.

Lukashenko used a landslide win in a referendum on November 24 to re-write the constitution, awarding himself sweeping powers over rival institutions, including the old parliament where many deputies opposed him.
But Lukashenko had promised deputies they would keep their rights even if they did not join the new chamber set up under his constitution and filled with his supporters.
Concerns run high in Poland about the situation in Belarus, and President Aleksander Kwasniewski has said he would grant asylum to political refugees from Belarus if necessary.
There was no evidence to suggest that Sharetsky was seeking political asylum.
Many Western officials and institutions have criticised Lukashenko for ignoring the old constitution and said the referendum itself was seriously flawed.
On Thursday the European Parliament urged the 15-nation European Union to stop financial aid to Belarus because of doubts over its commitment to democracy.
